title: LightPC Settings Schema
description: As the sole standard and specification for all settings, everything adheres to a unified standard.

appearence.description: Visual preferences: color mode, corner radius, palette and typography.

mode.description: Color mode requested by the user.

theme.description: Active palette and the palettes available to pick from.

default.description: Name of the palette used when nothing else is chosen.

palettes.description: Every palette the user can switch to. Derived data: it backs theme.default and the palette lookup.

light.description: Theme variables of this colour mode. Keys are the custom property names in camel case, so card-foreground is written as cardForeground.

dark.description: Theme variables of this colour mode. Keys are the custom property names in camel case, so card-foreground is written as cardForeground.

items.$comment: A user document may add a palette under a new name, or retune the colours of a shipped one. A shipped name merges key by key, so only the mentioned variables change.

theme.$comment: Uses rendererExtension: palettes is x-drived and default pulls its options from it.

default.description: Family used when nothing else is chosen. While useSystem is off the options are the bundled families; while it is on they come from the system font list.

useSystem.description: Include the fonts installed on the machine in the picker.

builtin.description: Families shipped with the application. Derived data: every entry must have a matching file under public/fonts, so the renderer never offers a font that cannot load.

general.description: Preferences that are not tied to a single feature.

availableLanguages.description: Locales the interface can switch to. Derived data: it backs general.language.

level.description: Lowest level the panel keeps. Every level at or above it is included, so "warn" shows warnings and errors.

availableLevels.description: Levels the console may show. Derived data: it backs log.level, so the options are configuration rather than a constant in the code.

refreshInterval.description: How often the rendered log is refreshed, written as "<number> <unit>" such as "1 s". The unit is chosen from the time set.

autoScroll.description: Keep the view anchored to the newest record as it arrives.

doNotDisturb.description: Silences the toast without touching what the engine records. Switching it on hides the popup while every notice keeps landing in the notification centre.

history.description: How many notices the notification centre shows. The backend keeps the left edge: once the ring holds more than this, the oldest ids fall out of the answer and clearing rewrites the edge.

fold.description: How many notices a single toast may stack before the rest collapse into a count. It is a display cap, not a record cap: the ones that did not fit are still in the centre.

duration.description: How long one toast stays on screen, written as "<number> <unit>" such as "5 s". The unit is chosen from the second, minute and hour, because a popup that stays for less than a second is not readable and one that stays for a day is forgotten.

position.description: Where a toast appears. The options come from the sibling availablePositions array.

availablePositions.description: The positions the picker offers. It sits beside position rather than inside the schema keyword so a document can narrow the list without editing the schema.

size.description: A length with an explicit unit, such as '8 px' or '1.5 rem'.

variables.description: Design tokens keyed by CSS custom property; values are raw CSS colors.

section.description: An open section whose keys are defined once the feature lands.
